facts.statement: Alvarezsaurus was discovered in the Bajo de la Carpa Formation and named by José Bonaparte in 1991 in honor of the historian Don Gregorio Alvarez.
facts.quote: It was found in the Bajo de la Carpa Formation and was named by paleontologist José Bonaparte in 1991 after the historian Don Gregorio Alvarez.

facts.statement: Alvarezsaurus lived in Argentina approximately 86 to 83 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: living in Argentina approximately 86 - 83 million years ago.

facts.statement: Alvarezsaurus was a small dinosaur measuring 1 to 1.4 meters in length and weighing approximately 3 kilograms.
facts.quote: It was a small dinosaur, measuring 1 - 1.4 m long and weighing approximately 3 kg.

facts.statement: Alvarezsaurus was a bipedal theropod dinosaur.
The leg structure of Alvarezsaurus suggests it was capable of running fast.
facts.quote: its leg structure suggests that it was a fast runner.

facts.statement: Alvarezsaurus was unique among its relatives for having metatarsal III as its longest foot bone, followed by an unusually long metatarsal IV.
facts.quote: It was unique in that its metatarsal III was its longest, followed by an unusually long metatarsal IV.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Alvarezsaurus may have been insectivorous.
Alvarezsaurus possessed a beak and developed feathers covering its body.
facts.quote: Poseía pico y un desarrollado plumaje recubriendo su cuerpo.

facts.statement: Alvarezsaurus had a beak with sharp teeth, indicating it was a carnivore that likely fed on lizards, insects, and small mammals.
facts.quote: Su pico poseía dientes filosos, lo que indica que era un carnívoro que probablemente se alimentaba de lagartos, insectos, mamíferos pequeños, etc.

facts.statement: Alvarezsaurus was not a large animal, reaching approximately 2 meters in length, nearly 1.1 meters in height, and weighing up to 20 kilograms.
facts.quote: Alvarezsaurus no era un animal grande: su longitud era de aproximadamente 2 metros y su altura de casi 1,1 metro, llegando a pesar 20 kilogramos.

facts.statement: Alvarezsaurus is considered a basal member of the Alvarezsauridae family, preceding better-known relatives like Mononykus and Shuvuuia.
facts.quote: Alvarezsaurus is considered basal to better-known members of its family, such as Mononykus and Shuvuuia.

facts.statement: Alvarezsaurus has been classified as either a non-avian theropod or a primitive bird, but the theory linking Alvarezsauridae closely to modern birds (neornithines) remains controversial despite earlier support.
facts.quote: Han sido clasificados desde terópodos no avianos a aves primitivas, pero una teoría de que Alvarezsauridae sea reconocida como más relacionada con las aves neornithes ha sido objeto de controversia a pesar de ser apoyado por estudios anteriores.

facts.statement: It was once believed that Patagonian Alvarezsaurus taxa were the most basal in their family, but this was refuted by the discovery of the more basal genus Haplocheirus in China.
facts.quote: Una vez se creyó que los taxones de alvarezsáuridos de la Patagonia eran los más basales de su familia, pero el descubrimiento de un miembro más basal, Haplocheirus, refutada cuando fueron descubiertos los fósiles Haplocheirus en China.

facts.statement: Alvarezsaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous, between 89 and 85 million years ago in the Coniacian stage, in what is now South America.
facts.quote: vivió a finales del período Cretácico, entre el 89 a 85 millones de años, durante el Coniaciense en lo que es hoy Sudamérica.

facts.statement: The fossil record for Alvarezsaurus dates from 85.7 to 83.6 million years ago during the Santonian age.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Santonian (85.7 to 83.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: The type specimen of Alvarezsaurus was discovered in March 1989 by Jorge Calvo while prospecting along the south coast of the Río Neuquén.
facts.quote: Una mañana del mes de marzo de 1989 Calvo decide hacer una prospección sobre la costa sur del Río Neuquén.

facts.statement: While bone fragments were common finds, the initial discovery involved a 5 cm long white bone fragment found near a light post.
facts.quote: Fragmentos de huesos eran los más comunes de encontrar, sin embargo, próximo a un poste de luz asomaba un huesito de 5 cm de largo de color blanco.

facts.statement: After uncovering part of the fossil, Jorge Calvo confirmed it was the leg of an animal with hollow bones.
facts.quote: Luego de destapar una parte comprobó que había una pata de un animal de huesos huecos.

facts.statement: In 1991, José Bonaparte published the description of Alvarezsaurus in the Revista del Museo de Ciencias Naturales de Buenos Aires, dedicating the species A. calvoi to Jorge Calvo.
facts.quote: Bonaparte posteriormente agradecería este gesto dedicándole la especie de Alvarezsaurus a Calvo, A. calvoi, en una publicación científica de la Revista del museo de Ciencias Naturales de Buenos Aires en 1991.
